findings.message: FR-009 says that after the story, a case-insensitive search for `resource[ _]?type` in backend/src finds only the historical migration files of earlier stories and their designer files. This new acceptance-test file still has one hit, in a doc comment. The comment itself claims the opposite: that the old names are built by concatenation so the search finds nothing in this file. No other file outside the migrations matches, and no production code or user-visible text is affected. Severity is MINOR, not BLOCKER, because FR-009 is a functional requirement and not an AC, decision or contract clause (AC-6, AC-7 and AC-13 do not cover test source). The file is a hashed acceptance-test file (red-first), so fixing it requires a rebaseline decision like DEC-7. Side note on the same rule: the story's own migration (20261007131957_RenameResourceTypeToResourceSchema.cs and its Designer) has to contain the old names in order to rename them. FR-009 as written ('earlier stories' only) does not allow for that. This is a gap in the spec text, not a code defect; the owner should widen FR-009 to include this story's migration.
findings.evidence: ResourcesApiDescriptionTests.cs:29: `/// the old name (FR-009) finds no hit in this file. "resource type" also covers "resource types";` (Grep `(?i)resource[ _]?type` over backend/src: hits only in Migrations/* and this line)
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the comment so it does not contain the old phrase. Apply this through the acceptance-test rebaseline path, because the file is hashed.

verification_notes: AC-1 / AC-2 / FR-001 / FR-003: ResourcesModule.cs maps all five schema operations only at /resources/schemas and /resources/schemas/{id:guid}. The operation names are Create/Get/Update/Delete resource schema(s), and POST returns Created(/resources/schemas/{id}, { id }). The /resources/types routes are removed and no alias is left. The instance list parameter, the create request and the row/single DTOs are renamed to ResourceSchemaId.
DEC-2: ResourcesExceptionToResponseMapper.cs:13 returns code RESOURCE_SCHEMA_NAME_TAKEN with the message unchanged.

AC-7: all six messages from the spec's message list are updated word for word in the handlers. Check order is unchanged (empty-name check before the owner check in CreateResourceSchemaCommandHandler). No 'resource type' text is left in Resources production code.

AC-8 / DEC-4: the three texts are changed exactly as specified (resources-panel.component.html:33, schemas-panel.component.html:22 and :53). The sign-in slogan is kept (auth-page.component.html:33). The service, store, modal, detail page and schema designer use /resources/schemas and resourceSchemaId. frontend/src has no other old-name hits.

AC-9 / AC-13 / DEC-1 / DEC-6: the migration is rename-only (RenameTable, RenameColumn x2, RenameIndex x2) plus drop/re-add of the PK and FK. The FK name FK_resource_property_definitions_resource_schemas matches ResourceSchemaConfiguration.HasConstraintName and the model snapshot. InitResources has no other old-name object, so nothing is left unrenamed.

Contract: the routes, request models, the resourceSchemaId field and the query parameter match contract-next.json. The generated client files under frontend/src/app/api were fully regenerated per DEC-8, so the unrelated ManagementGroups/ProblemDetails changes are covered by that decision and not reported.

No weak assertion found: the AC-2, AC-6, AC-7, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12, AC-13, AC-9/14 and AC-8 tests assert status, code, message, body and database state tightly enough that a violation of their AC would fail them.
Outside the diff, not a code finding: generated/capability-map.json still names /resources/types. It is a generated artifact; regenerate it at close.
